description.narrative: This project, CoDA will select farmers to participate in consultations and provide information on the status of industrial crop cultivation, build understanding of the current situation, study, and find ways to develop and utilize their skills to adapt to changing natural disasters. The Community Development Association (CoDA) will consult with the government, business units, or relevant entrepreneurs to find ways to jointly develop and mitigate potential impacts from their operations. This is to contribute to social development alongside business operations. The problem-solving approach will start from the grassroots or bottom-up, beginning with the villages and households involved with eucalyptus plantations first. Coordination and data collection on impacts will be done with village heads and their spouses, including women and youth in the target villages. Furthermore, village authorities, relevant divisions and sectors from the district and province will also coordinate to implement activities successfully: - The Community Development Association (CoDA) will collaborate with Savannakhet University (SKU) to jointly study and analyze data for implementing this sub-project's activities. - The Community Development Association (CoDA) will coordinate with relevant state organizations and entrepreneurs to discuss the feasibility of drafting policies or strategies for developing villages impacted by cassava and eucalyptus cultivation in the target villages. - A workshop will be organized at the provincial level to consider, define key activities, and draft a policy requiring the private sector involved in eucalyptus planting to have obligations, share responsibility for impacts, and participate in village development to mitigate the effects of their eucalyptus plantations. - The final binding policy document will be signed at the provincial governor level for dissemination, printing, and monitoring of implementation together with the Modern Agriculture Project, with entrepreneurs also agreeing and signing the commitment to mitigate impacts in the target areas. - Support the formation of model groups at the village level in Pak Kouay and Khamtonglong villages, Champhone District, consisting of 2 sub-groups, to improve livelihoods and reduce impacts from industrial crop cultivation. There will be monitoring and support for the operations of these village-level model groups. CoDA will provide information, knowledge, and experience to villagers regarding industrial cropand tree planting, helping them understand the advantages and disadvantages of such activities. Through coordination and collaboration with the government and community in studying and analyzing data, the local conditions, including strengths, weaknesses, challenges, and various problemsaffecting community livelihoods, will be summarized. These findings will then be discussed with entrepreneurs regarding the feasibility of defining policies or strategies for local development to mitigate the impacts of eucalyptus plantingin the next phase. Knowledge and understanding of local conditions, advantages, disadvantages, challenges, and problems in industrial crop and tree planting can be used for discussions among the government, entrepreneurs, and the community to find ways for improvementand resolution that all relevant parties can agree upon. This can become a joint policy or strategy that everyone will implement together for mutual benefit and success. The Community Development Association (CoDA) will act as a mediator and continue tooperate, contributing to helping the community, entrepreneurs, and the government in developing local collaboration. New knowledge and experience in promoting policies to mitigate the impacts of industrial crop and tree planting activities, especially eucalyptus, will help generate income for the community, and CoDA can leverage this to develop new projects in the next phase.

participating-org.narrative: Vision of the Association: CoDA have prosperous and happy lives through sustainable development and the participation of both womenand men. Mission: The Community Development Association (CoDA) is committed to developing and promoting production linked to sustainable markets, enhancing gender roles in participatory development, encouraging communities to access basic education and primary healthcare, and strengthening the association and partner organizations comprehensively. Objectives: - Communities/people have sufficient and safe food and stable income within a sound environment and natural resources. - Women and youth are equally recognized, receive opportunities, and have the capacity in decision-making processes for community development. - People in target groups can access basic education, health information, clean water, and consume a nutritionally complete diet. Main Activities: - Support activitiesfor food security and nutrition. - Promote natural resource and environmental management. - Strengthen women and youth. - Promote education and primary healthcare. - Engage in organizational learning and development to build strength. The Community Development Association (CoDA) is a social organization composed of regular members who voluntarily participate in development and provide supportto the organization. Currently, there are a total of 35 regular members (10 women), 7 full-time staff members, and 3 technical advisors. The Association consists of a 5-member Executive Board elected every 5 years (1 President, 2 Vice-Presidents, and 2 Committee Members), and a 3-member Inspection Committee elected from the regular members by the General Assembly every 5 years. The Association also has policies, regulations, and operating manuals for organizing and implementing work systematically and systematically. These policies and regulations include: Overall Association Policies, including: , Gender Policy, Child and Youth Rights Policy, Policy towards Third Gender Individuals, Anti-Fraud, Bribery, and Corruption Policy,. Personnel Management Regulations, including:, Employment conditions and labor contracts, Professional disciplinary regulations (verbal warning/formal warning/dismissal for serious misconduct), Fundraising Procedures andRegulations, Fundraising through project proposal writing, Fundraising through mobilization/voluntary donations, Income generation activities The Association was registered and received permanent approval on 29/10/2013 and can operate activities throughout the Lao PDR. The Association has previously implemented projects related to agricultural policy advocacy,and/or environmental issues and/or community development. The Association has experience in promoting policies to strengthen genderrelations, particularly in poor communities and Bru ethnic villages in Chonnaboury District. We believe this experience can be leveraged for the success of this project.
